body: Financials need their own tests (IL&FS, DHFL, Yes Bank, RCap, Lehman, SVB, Credit Suisse): (1) Funding: share of CP/short-term wholesale funding; ALM gap in the 1-year bucket (DHFL, IL&FS); uninsured/bulk deposit share and depositor concentration (SVB ~90%+, Yes Bank low CASA). (2) Asset quality: RBI divergence disclosures (Yes Bank FY16-17), restructured + SMA-2 book, loans to promoter-group or 'general purpose corporate loans' (RHFL), wholesale/developer concentration. (3) Growth: loan growth >30%/yr for several years in corporate books. (4) Capital: leverage (Lehman ~30x; NBFCs >7-8x), Level 3/model-marked assets vs equity, fair-value of HTM securities vs equity (SVB losses ~= equity). (5) Market: CP/bond spread spikes, CDS (Credit Suisse Oct 2022), rating outlooks; (6) Governance: regulator actions on CEO (Yes Bank), auditor exits (RCap PwC), material weakness opinions (CS), CRO vacancies (SVB). (7) Window-dressing: quarter-end vs average balance sheet (Repo 105). Rule: a lender trading at a discount to book with any two of these is pricing hidden losses -- avoid; equity is a thin slice (10x leverage means a 10% asset loss wipes it).

data.rule: two+ flags + discount to book = avoid

title: Banks/NBFCs: blow-up signals (M/Z-scores don't apply)

body: Builds on insight:disqualifiers-v2-proposal (unchanged) after the survivorship-free Indian back-test (insight:bt-hard-filters-india-v2-2026-summary). HARD AT ENTRY (unchanged from v2, judgment-only, untestable mechanically): H1a fake cash, H1b implausible economics after a written unit-economics check, H1c unverifiable profits, H4 pump patterns, H5 related-party leakage, H2 auditor exit over disagreement/qualified opinion, H3 rating not cooperating. HARD AT EXIT (unchanged): H2 and the strongest accounting-trouble events. GRADED RED (override template): promoter pledge >50% of promoter holding = strong (written override must state why, the lender, margin-call price vs current price) - tested lift 2.43 [1.65,3.47], 5.9% of winners; pledge >25% = red - lift 2.13 [1.53,2.94], 8.5% of winners; rising pledge >=10pp in a year = escalate (13 cases, untested); accounting-trouble events, dilution, solvency set as before (S1/S5 India = questions-leaning-red per L27). COMBINATION: pledge plus interest cover <1.5x = main 'look much harder, size small' prompt (post-hoc, needs forward check; the two overlap ~60%, so do not count them as independent votes). QUESTIONS, NOT FLAGS (confirmed on survivorship-free data): CFO/PAT 5y (<0.3 lift 2.08, CI 0.57-3.85, 11% of winners), debt growth with negative CFO (0.83), other-income share (1.36), debtor-day jumps (1.51; judge by counterparty). NO MECHANICAL ANY-FLAG GATE: ANY of the five flags 47% of later >=3x winners for lift 1.31. MOVED TO STAGE 5 (unchanged): P/E. Nothing mechanical is hard. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: pledge >50% lift >=4 on O_fail with CI >1 in a later snapshot set (2020, 2022) would make it hard; a forward record showing pledge overrides lose money would tighten the override.
title: PROPOSAL (not adopted): disqualifiers v3 - v2 structure kept; promoter pledge promoted to the top graded red flag with numeric levels (>25% red, >50% strong red, rising = escalate); cash-flow tells confirmed as questions; no mechanical any-flag gate
